recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Further edits would reopen policy already settled by FHIR-20770, FHIR-23840, FHIR-24661, and FHIR-38783 rather than apply the published FHIR-23840 decision.
issue_request: FHIR-23840 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care change request asking that Communication and CommunicationRequest explain why payload.content[x] can be a CodeableConcept, including the machine-generated finite-terminology use case, contentCodeableConcept.text for uncoded text, and the rule that the CodeableConcept is the communicated content rather than a categorization.
initial_application: The Jira application comment points to GitHub commit 43fcc3d. Git history confirms 43fcc3d1fec8c0bed029f0a85650fcb3913991d4 updated the then-authoritative Communication and CommunicationRequest spreadsheets with the requested explanatory comment. Commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 carried that comment into the current StructureDefinition XML during the 2021 source rework, and commit 086649a2357c29f8c83dca7604dc592d32c84355 added the same CommunicationRequest comment to mapping-exception source.
additional_context: FHIR-20770 introduced CodeableConcept payload support and the original non-categorization rule. FHIR-24661 later rejected adding a separate payload categorization element and quoted this same guidance as intended R5 behavior. FHIR-38783 revisited CommunicationRequest string/code concerns in 2024 but preserved the CodeableConcept guidance while changing only the CommunicationRequest payload definition wording. source/fhir.ini lists both communication and communicationrequest as active resources.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current Communication.payload.content[x] and CommunicationRequest.payload.content[x] both contain the requested comment, both still allow CodeableConcept as a content type, and the CommunicationRequest request-pattern mapping exception mirrors the comment.

related_jiras.note: Introduced CodeableConcept payload support and the initial rule that the CodeableConcept is communicated content, not categorization.
Rejected a separate payload categorization element and quoted the FHIR-23840 guidance as intended behavior.
Revisited CommunicationRequest string/code concerns and updated the payload definition while preserving the explanatory comment.
